blockMcqs.question: What separates continuous delivery from continuous deployment?
options: Delivery skips testing; deployment adds it
Delivery keeps changes deploy-ready; deployment auto-ships to prod
Deployment only runs in staging environments
Delivery requires canaries; deployment requires blue-green
blockMcqs.explanation: Delivery stops at a human button; deployment removes that human entirely.

blockMcqs.question: Why are unit tests run before end-to-end tests in a pipeline?
options: Unit tests need a deployed environment
E2E tests are more reliable so run last
To fail fast — cheap checks catch bugs first
Pipelines forbid mixing test types
blockMcqs.explanation: Spending 20 minutes on E2E when a 2-second unit test would catch it wastes the loop.

blockMcqs.question: Why rebuild the artifact only once and promote those exact bytes?
options: Rebuilding is too slow for staging
A rebuild can pull a different dependency than you tested
Registries reject duplicate version tags
It halves the number of pipeline stages
blockMcqs.explanation: Per-environment rebuilds risk drift, so staging would verify something other than what ships.

blockMcqs.question: A change breaks the existing API contract. Which version bump?
options: PATCH
MINOR
MAJOR
No bump needed
blockMcqs.explanation: Breaking compatibility forces callers to update, which is exactly what MAJOR signals.

blockMcqs.question: What does a feature flag let you decouple?
options: The build from the test stage
The deploy from the user-facing release
The artifact from its version tag
The runner from the registry
blockMcqs.explanation: Code can sit in prod turned off, so shipping it and releasing it become separate events.

blockMcqs.question: Which strategy gives the smallest blast radius for a risky change?
options: Rolling
Blue-green
Canary
Big-bang
blockMcqs.explanation: Routing a tiny slice first and widening on healthy metrics limits exposure most tightly.

blockMcqs.question: Why use expand/contract migrations during a rollout?
options: They run faster than single-step migrations
Old and new code must coexist while both versions serve traffic
They avoid touching the registry
They eliminate the need for backups
blockMcqs.explanation: Rolling and canary keep both versions live, so the schema must satisfy each at once.

blockMcqs.question: Why compare a canary against the live baseline, not a fixed number?
options: Fixed thresholds are illegal in canaries
Traffic patterns vary by time of day
The baseline runs in a separate cluster
It avoids needing observability tooling
blockMcqs.explanation: Absolute limits misfire when normal load shifts; relative comparison adapts to current traffic.

blockMcqs.question: Which DORA metric measures how fast you recover from a bad change?
options: Deployment frequency
Lead time for changes
Change-failure rate
Mean time to recovery
blockMcqs.explanation: MTTR is the stability metric that justifies investing in instant rollback and fast detection.

blockMcqs.question: When is "rollback is just redeploying the old version" wrong?
options: When the artifact is in a registry
When an irreversible migration already ran
When using semantic versioning
When the pipeline is defined as code
blockMcqs.explanation: Old code can't understand a schema a one-way migration already changed.
